title: DXA BONE DENSITOMETRY, AXIAL SKELETON
author: Martin Osei, MD
impression:
1. Osteoporosis, lowest T-score -2.9 at the lumbar spine.
2. Statistically significant 4.1% decline in lumbar spine BMD since 09/2024 despite alendronate therapy.
3. High 10-year fracture risk by FRAX.

sections.heading: Indication
sections.text: Age-related osteoporosis on alendronate since 2020. Prior right femoral neck fracture. Follow-up.

sections.heading: Findings
sections.text:
Region BMD (g/cm²) T-score Z-score Change vs 2024
Lumbar spine L1-L4 0.712 -2.9 -0.9 -4.1% (significant)
Left femoral neck 0.556 -2.6 -0.4 -1.2% (not significant)
Left total hip 0.648 -2.3 -0.3 -0.9% (not significant)
Right hip not scanned (prior fracture fixation hardware). No vertebral levels excluded.
FRAX 10-year probability (femoral neck BMD): major osteoporotic fracture 24%, hip fracture 7.8%.

sections.heading: Impression
sections.text:
1. Osteoporosis, lowest T-score -2.9 at the lumbar spine.
2. Statistically significant 4.1% decline in lumbar spine BMD since 09/2024 despite alendronate therapy.
3. High 10-year fracture risk by FRAX.

sections.heading: Recommendations
sections.text:
Consider evaluation for secondary causes of bone loss and review of adherence and treatment (e.g., anabolic or parenteral therapy).
Repeat DXA in 2 years on the same scanner.
